identity.what_it_is: An urban beach park on English Bay in the West End neighbourhood of Vancouver, British Columbia, part of the city seawall system, adjacent to the Vancouver Aquatic Centre.
identity.where: Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada (foot of Bute/Thurlow, English Bay, West End)
identity.warnings: Do not conflate with 'Sunset, Vancouver' (an unrelated South Vancouver neighbourhood), any Sunset Beach in California/Hawaii/North Carolina/Ontario, the 'Summer Village of Sunset Beach' (a small unrelated BC municipality), or 'Sunset Towers' (an unrelated social-housing building). A second Indigenous name, hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓ 'ʔəy̓əlxən', is claimed in scout notes but was NOT found in any harvested source text -- unverified, treat as a dead end.

spike_candidates.statement: A 61-metre barge that broke loose and washed ashore at Sunset Beach on November 15, 2021 became a beloved local landmark before a delayed, $2.4 million removal completed in late 2022.
spike_candidates.tension: Bureaucratic delay over a goose nest and lead-paint contamination in the hull let a viral 'celebrity' barge sit on a public beach for roughly a year before the city spent $2.4 million to remove it.

spike_candidates.statement: The Sunset Beach AIDS Memorial, unveiled in December 2004 after an eight-year fight against homophobic opposition to its siting, now bears the names of hundreds of British Columbians who died of AIDS.
spike_candidates.tension: Even the sources documenting this beloved memorial can't agree on its basic facts -- 16 panels vs. 20, and roughly 800 names vs. 996 -- showing how loosely the record has been kept for a monument that took a decade to fund and build.

spike_candidates.statement: Sunset Beach's water has been closed to swimming for high E. coli counts at least twice in recent memory (2018 and 2022), under a Vancouver Coastal Health monitoring system built on sewage and stormwater runoff triggers.
spike_candidates.tension: A beach marketed for lifeguarded summer swimming sits downstream of the same storm-drain and sewage-overflow mechanism that periodically shuts it to swimmers, and the city's own official beach page (403) and both 2026 CBC stories on this year's closures could not be fetched, so how current the risk is right now is unverifiable from this source set.

spike_candidates.statement: A woman's body was found floating in the water at Sunset Beach on July 21, 2024, later identified as 29-year-old singer Karen Musumadi.
spike_candidates.tension: Vancouver Police described the cause of death as undetermined at the time, and no harvested source confirms whether a final ruling was ever issued -- this needs careful, non-sensational handling if used at all, and arguably shouldn't anchor a beach profile.

facts.fact: Sunset Beach is an urban beach park on English Bay in Vancouver's West End neighbourhood.
facts.quote: sunset beach is an urban beach park on english bay situated in the west end neighbourhood of vancouver , british columbia, canada.
facts.source_title: Sunset Beach (Vancouver) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The beach is part of the city seawall and is bisected by a multi-use path linking it to the Vancouver Aquatic Centre and the Burrard Street Bridge.
facts.quote: it is part of the city seawall system and is bisected by a multi-use path for bicycling, walking, and skating that connects to the adjacent vancouver aquatic centre and burrard street bridge .
facts.source_title: Sunset Beach (Vancouver) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The city-maintained park includes public washrooms, concession stands, an off-leash dog area, and a False Creek Ferries dock.
facts.quote: the park is maintained by the city government and includes public washrooms, concession stands, an off-leash area for dogs, and a false creek ferries dock.
facts.source_title: Sunset Beach (Vancouver) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Lifeguards are posted at Sunset Beach between May and September.
facts.quote: between may and september, lifeguards are posted at the beach.
facts.source_title: Sunset Beach (Vancouver) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The beach hosted an unofficial 4/20 protest annually on April 20 in the late 2010s.
facts.quote: the beach hosted an unofficial 420 protest annually on april 20 in the late 2010s.
facts.source_title: Sunset Beach (Vancouver) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Sunset Beach is a popular spot for watching the Celebration of Light annual fireworks display.
facts.quote: it is a popular location for watching celebration of light , an annual fireworks display.
facts.source_title: Sunset Beach (Vancouver) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The beach's Squamish-language Indigenous name is Í7iy̓el̓shn, meaning "soft underfoot."
facts.quote: the beach's indigenous name is í7iy̓el̓shn ("ee-ay-ul-shun"), which means "soft underfoot" in the squamish language .
facts.source_title: Sunset Beach (Vancouver) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: On November 15, 2021, a 61-metre (200 ft) barge broke free during regional floods and washed ashore at Sunset Beach.
facts.quote: on november 15, 2021, a 61-metre (200 ft) barge washed ashore at sunset beach during regional floods after it broke free from its moored position.
facts.source_title: Sunset Beach (Vancouver) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Nicknamed a "celebrity," the stranded barge became a local landmark that inspired memes, songs, and parodies.
facts.quote: described as a "celebrity", the barge became a local landmark that inspired memes , songs, and parodies.
facts.source_title: Sunset Beach (Vancouver) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Approval to dismantle the barge, first proposed in January 2022, was delayed by the discovery of a goose nest and concern over lead contamination in the hull paint.
facts.quote: proposals to dismantle the barge were first submitted in january 2022, but approval was delayed due to the discovery of a goose nest and concerns of lead contamination from the hull paint among other issues.
facts.source_title: Sunset Beach (Vancouver) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Barge removal began July 25, 2022 and finished over three months later at a cost of $2.4 million.
facts.quote: removal began on july 25, 2022, and was completed over three months later at a cost of $2.4 million.
facts.source_title: Sunset Beach (Vancouver) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Sunset Beach Park, established in 1959, completed a continuous strip of public waterfront between Stanley Park and the head of False Creek.
facts.quote: sunset beach park, established in 1959, completed the dream of a continuous strip of public waterfront between stanley park and the head of false creek.
facts.source_title: Sunset Beach Park - Places That Matter

facts.fact: In 1941 businessman George C. Reifel traded a 198-foot strip of property at the foot of Bute Street to the city, enabling the seawall park plan to proceed.
facts.quote: in 1941, businessman george c. reifel traded a crucial 198 foot strip of property at the foot of bute street to the city for property elsewhere, enabling the plan to move forward.
facts.source_title: Sunset Beach Park - Places That Matter

facts.fact: The last waterfront building, the 1928 Crystal Pool at the foot of Jervis, was demolished once the Vancouver Aquatic Centre opened in 1974.
facts.quote: the last building on the waterfront, the 1928 crystal pool at the foot of jervis, was demolished once the vancouver aquatic centre opened in 1974.
facts.source_title: Sunset Beach Park - Places That Matter

facts.fact: The 1941 land swap valued the Reifels' three lots at $15,035 against a $23,700 Granville Street property, with the Reifels also paying $8,665 into the city's sinking fund.
facts.quote: the reifels gave the city three lots on the southwest corner of beach and bute (assessed at $15,035) in exchange for a business property on granville street near davie, assessed at $23,700, and paid $8,665 into the city's sinking fund.
facts.source_title: Sunset Beach Park - Places That Matter

facts.fact: An estimated 40,000 people attended the 4/20 rally at Sunset Beach in 2017.
facts.quote: an estimated 40,000 people attended the 4/20 rally in 2017.
facts.source_title: Sunset Beach Park - Places That Matter

facts.fact: The AIDS Memorial's ribbon of 20 corten-steel panels is engraved with the names of nearly 800 British Columbians who died of AIDS.
facts.quote: the ribbon of steel is composed of 20 steel panels anchored to concrete piers and is engraved with the names of nearly 800 people from bc who have died of aids.
facts.source_title: AIDS Memorial - Public Art Registry, City of Vancouver

facts.fact: The AIDS Memorial's artist is Bruce Wilson, installed as a gift to the city in 2004.
facts.quote: artist(s) bruce wilson
facts.source_title: AIDS Memorial - Public Art Registry, City of Vancouver

facts.fact: It took 10 years to raise the funds needed to build the AIDS Memorial.
facts.quote: it took 10 years to raise the funds.
facts.source_title: AIDS Memorial - Public Art Registry, City of Vancouver

facts.fact: The memorial's design was selected from over 70 submissions to a public call for designs.
facts.quote: the design was chosen from over 70 submissions to a public call for designs.
facts.source_title: AIDS Memorial - Public Art Registry, City of Vancouver

facts.fact: The Vancouver AIDS Memorial took eight years to complete, delayed by bureaucracy and public opposition sometimes fuelled by homophobia.
facts.quote: vancouver's aids memorial took eight years to complete, mired from the outset in bureaucratic red tape and a lengthy public process sometimes fuelled by homophobia
facts.source_title: The man behind the monument - Xtra Magazine

facts.fact: One account describes the memorial as 16 metal panels curved like a ribbon, conflicting with the City's own 20-panel description.
facts.quote: there are 16 metal panels curved like a ribbon of metal.
facts.source_title: The man behind the monument - Xtra Magazine

facts.fact: As of 2005, an estimated five to seven million people a year walked the seawall past the memorial.
facts.quote: five to seven million people a year walk the seawall,
facts.source_title: The man behind the monument - Xtra Magazine

facts.fact: As of 2005 there was room for 200 more names on two empty memorial panels.
facts.quote: there's room for 200 more names on two empty panels.
facts.source_title: The man behind the monument - Xtra Magazine

facts.fact: By 2010 a visitor's account put the memorial's tally at 996 names, higher than the City's later 'nearly 800.'
facts.quote: vancouver aids memorial since 1 december 2004 996 names
facts.source_title: Vancouver AIDS Memorial - aidsmemorial.info

facts.fact: This source also describes 20 steel panels joined together with names cut into the metal, matching the City's registry but not Xtra's account of 16.
facts.quote: the structure is made up of 20 steel panels joined together, with names of individuals who lost their lives to aids cut into the metal.
facts.source_title: Vancouver AIDS Memorial - aidsmemorial.info

facts.fact: The memorial's final panel bears a quote from Dr. Peter, a Vancouver physician and AIDS activist who died of the disease in 1992: "the energy that is me will not be lost."
facts.quote: but the energy that is me will not be lost .
facts.source_title: Vancouver AIDS Memorial - aidsmemorial.info

facts.fact: On July 16, 2022, repeat samples at Sunset Beach showed E. coli counts exceeding 862 per 100 mL, well above the safety limit.
facts.quote: repeat single samples of water off sunset beach showed e. coli counts exceeding 862 per 100 millilitres.
facts.source_title: Sunset Beach and English Bay closed to swimming - Georgia Straight

facts.fact: The single-sample E. coli safety limit for swimming is under 400 per 100 mL; Sunset Beach's 2022 reading of 862 was more than double that.
facts.quote: that's far above the single sample limit of less than 400 e. coli per 100 millilitres.
facts.source_title: Sunset Beach and English Bay closed to swimming - Georgia Straight

facts.fact: On August 11, 2018, Vancouver Coastal Health warned against swimming at English Bay, Sunset Beach, and Jericho Beach due to high bacteria counts.
facts.quote: on august 11, vancouver coastal health (vch) issued a health warning, advising against wading and swimming at english bay, sunset beach, and jericho beach due to high bacteria counts found at those locations.
facts.source_title: Vancouver's English Bay and Sunset Beach reopen to swimming - Georgia Straight

facts.fact: As of August 9, 2018, E. coli counts were 185/100 mL at English Bay and 232/100 mL at Sunset Beach, against a 200/100 mL recreational-safety guideline; the advisory was lifted August 14, 2018.
facts.quote: as of august 9, bacteria counts at english bay were 185 e. coli per 100 millilitres of water while sunset beach was at 232.
facts.source_title: Vancouver's English Bay and Sunset Beach reopen to swimming - Georgia Straight

facts.fact: Since 2023, Vancouver Coastal Health triggers a contamination investigation when a single sample exceeds 235 E. coli/100 mL, down from the prior 400/100 mL threshold.
facts.quote: the key change is if a single sample exceeds 235 e.coli/100 ml (as opposed to 400 e.coli/100 ml prior to 2023), a contamination investigation, and resampling will be triggered.
facts.source_title: Public Beach Water Quality - Vancouver Coastal Health

facts.fact: VCH lists heavy rain runoff, sewage system overflows, leaking septic tanks, and boat discharge as the main sources of beach E. coli contamination.
facts.quote: there are many possible sources of e.coli contamination. heavy rain and subsequent surface runoff from contaminated sources sewage system overflows leaking septic tanks, and discharge from boats.
facts.source_title: Public Beach Water Quality - Vancouver Coastal Health

facts.fact: On July 21, 2024, Vancouver police responded after a woman's body was found in the water at Sunset Beach.
facts.quote: investigators and a white tent are pictured at sunset beach on sunday, july 21.
facts.source_title: Woman found dead in the water near Sunset Beach: Vancouver police - CTV News

facts.fact: The woman found in the water was identified as 29-year-old singer Karen Musumadi.
facts.quote: the woman has been identified as 29-year-old karen musumadi.
facts.source_title: Remembering Karen Musumadi - BC Community Alliance

facts.fact: Vancouver police said the cause of Karen Musumadi's death had yet to be determined, with no evidence of foul play at that time.
facts.quote: sgt. steve addison from the vancouver police department noted the complexity of the case, mentioning that the cause of death has yet to be determined.
facts.source_title: Remembering Karen Musumadi - BC Community Alliance

facts.fact: Vancouver's 2026 fireworks show, "Summer Lights in English Bay," is a single one-night event on July 31, 2026, replacing the traditional three-night Honda Celebration of Light.
facts.quote: the city of vancouver's "summer lights in english bay" event will take place this friday, july 31, 2026, offering a single night of fireworks in place of the traditional three-night honda celebration of light international fireworks competition.
facts.source_title: Everything you need to know about Vancouver's English Bay fireworks - Daily Hive

facts.fact: The 2026 Honda Celebration of Light was cancelled in late 2025 after organizers could not secure funding to cover a shortfall and rising costs.
facts.quote: the 2026 honda celebration of light was cancelled in late 2025 , after organizers were unable to secure timely government and private-sector funding to cover its projected shortfall and rising costs.
facts.source_title: Everything you need to know about Vancouver's English Bay fireworks - Daily Hive

facts.fact: The 2026 fireworks display runs 25 minutes starting at 10 p.m., launched from a barge in the middle of English Bay.
facts.quote: the fireworks will have the usual runtime of 25 minutes and begin at the traditional start time of precisely 10 p.m., launched from a barge positioned in the middle of english bay.
facts.source_title: Everything you need to know about Vancouver's English Bay fireworks - Daily Hive

facts.fact: The fireworks are best viewed from English Bay Beach, Sunset Beach Park, the Stanley Park seawall, Vanier Park, and Kitsilano Beach.
facts.quote: the fireworks will be best viewed from english bay beach, sunset beach park, and the stanley park seawall, as well as from vanier park and kitsilano beach across the water.
facts.source_title: Everything you need to know about Vancouver's English Bay fireworks - Daily Hive

facts.fact: The adjacent Vancouver Aquatic Centre permanently closed on June 28, 2026 after 52 years of operation, following a BC Supreme Court interim injunction.
facts.quote: due to the supreme court of british columbia interim injunction, the centre permanently closed on 28 june, 2026 after 52 years of operation.
facts.source_title: Vancouver Aquatic Centre - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The aging Aquatic Centre is being demolished and replaced by a $175 million facility with a much smaller 25-metre pool.
facts.quote: the aging building is currently undergoing demolition and will be replaced within a few years with a more modern $175 million facility with a much smaller 25 metre pool and other amenities.
facts.source_title: Vancouver Aquatic Centre - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The Aquatic Centre's predecessor, the 1928 Crystal Pool, racially segregated Asian and Black swimmers to one day a week until 1945, which gave the nearby False Creek Indian Reserve beach the informal name "Brown Skin Beach."
facts.quote: because of racial segregation at the pool from its beginning in 1928 until 1945, which allowed oriental and brown-skinned people to swim at the pool only one day a week, the nearby indian reserve beach at false creek became informally known as "brown skin beach".
facts.source_title: Vancouver Aquatic Centre - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The West End neighbourhood surrounding Sunset Beach sits between Coal Harbour and downtown to the east, Stanley Park to the northwest, English Bay to the west, and Kitsilano across False Creek to the southwest.
facts.quote: the west end is a neighbourhood in vancouver , british columbia, canada, located between the coal harbour neighbourhood and the financial and central business districts of downtown vancouver to the east, stanley park to the northwest, the english bay to the west, and kitsilano to the southwest across the false creek opening.
facts.source_title: West End, Vancouver - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The West End land was purchased in 1862 by John Morton, Samuel Brighouse, and William Hailstone, nicknamed the "three greenhorn Englishmen."
facts.quote: the area was purchased in 1862 by john morton, samuel brighouse, and william hailstone, three men known as the "three greenhorn englishmen"
facts.source_title: West End, Vancouver - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Babylon Cafe, a few blocks inland on Denman Street, is recommended specifically for assembling a beach picnic for English Bay/Sunset Beach.
facts.quote: looking for food for a beach picnic at nearby english bay? pop by babylon cafe for a huge range of mediterranean food.
facts.source_title: Dished neighbourhood gems: Vancouver's West End - Daily Hive

facts.fact: Tavola, a neighbourhood Italian restaurant on Robson Street near Denman, is known for hand-made pasta dishes in the West End.
facts.quote: on robson street just off of denman, tavola has some of the best hand-made pasta dishes in the city
facts.source_title: Dished neighbourhood gems: Vancouver's West End - Daily Hive

facts.fact: For the April 20, 2025 informal 4/20 gathering, the city stationed park rangers, VPD officers, and protective services at Sunset Beach Park and Thornton Park for public safety.
facts.quote: park rangers, vpd officers, and city protective services will be at sunset beach park and thornton park on sunday, april 20, 2025, for public safety.
facts.source_title: Vancouver 420 event 2025 - Vancouver Is Awesome

facts.fact: For the 2025 4/20 event, the Sunset Beach parking lot was closed from Saturday evening through Sunday and vehicle access closed until Easter Monday.
facts.quote: the sunset beach parking lot will be closed from saturday evening through sunday.
facts.source_title: Vancouver 420 event 2025 - Vancouver Is Awesome
